subject.title: [Feature]: Track data provenance across session boundaries for persistent state

question: What minimal durable provenance contract should OpenClaw expose across tool results, persistent writes, and future reads, and which metadata is safe for ordinary versus trusted plugins?
rationale: The answer defines a public Plugin SDK security boundary, persisted metadata shape, legacy-state behavior, read-time policy, and plugin visibility rules that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Design the durable provenance API first
options.body: Define the metadata contract, visibility rules, legacy unknown-provenance behavior, and validation plan before implementation work starts.

options.title: Land prerequisite hook slices first
options.body: Use issues #48503 and #48509 to add narrower hook context first while keeping this issue open for the durable chain and read-time policy.

options.title: Defer to plugin-specific implementations
options.body: Close or narrow this only if maintainers decide current Plugin SDK seams are sufficient and durable provenance should live outside core.

recommendation.title: Design the durable provenance API first
recommendation.body: Define the metadata contract, visibility rules, legacy unknown-provenance behavior, and validation plan before implementation work starts.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent provenance/session history makes them the best available owner for deciding the security boundary before implementation.
